title: Leveraging the PACE Plan into the Emergency Communications Ecosystem
finding: Primary/Alternate/Contingency/Emergency should be feasible, acceptable, suitable, distinguishable and complete
rust_boy_implication: Model a failure-domain-separated PACE registry, explicit escalation triggers and operator drills
limitations: CISA guidance is operational, not a proof of transport reliability

title: 2024 NCSWIC PACE Plan emergency communications ecosystem
finding: PACE layers cannot share the outage's underlying transmission medium; both sides need a usable option
rust_boy_implication: Require independent failure domains and endpoint capabilities for each tier
limitations: No evidence of installed alternate radios or modems on Rust-Boy

title: SP 800-34 Rev. 1 — Contingency Planning Guide
finding: Document topology, vendors, recovery workflows, monitoring and single points of failure
rust_boy_implication: Build dependency map and recovery checklist for peer transport, DNS, power and storage
limitations: Broad federal guidance; local implementation varies

title: SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP-8 Telecommunications Services
finding: Alternate telecommunications must reduce shared single points of failure and meet continuity need
rust_boy_implication: Document ISP/cell carrier/backhaul/power correlations, capacity and service objectives
limitations: Control selection must be tailored; no automatic conformance

title: National Emergency Communications Plan
finding: Interoperability needs governance, procedures, training, cybersecurity and exercise evidence
rust_boy_implication: Keep human procedures, cross-device compatibility and periodic failover tests with the code
limitations: Not a product specification or software certification

title: RFC 4838 — Delay-Tolerant Networking Architecture
finding: Store-and-forward messages survive disconnected endpoints and variable delays
rust_boy_implication: Plan persistent envelope, TTL, hop count, deduplication and explicit custody semantics
limitations: Architecture, not deployable Rust library or full security profile

title: RFC 9171 — Bundle Protocol Version 7
finding: Bundles provide store-carry-forward under intermittent and asymmetric links
rust_boy_implication: Evaluate BPv7 as interoperable option behind transport adapter; do not assume implemented
limitations: BPv7 requires additional convergence layers and operational design

title: RFC 9172 — Bundle Protocol Security (BPSec)
finding: DTN traffic needs integrity/confidentiality across untrusted intermediate storage
rust_boy_implication: Make message security independent of carrier and protect store-and-forward envelopes
limitations: BPSec roles and keying need careful profile design; not E2EE by default

title: RFC 9420 — Messaging Layer Security
finding: Asynchronous group messaging can achieve forward secrecy and post-compromise security with managed group epochs
rust_boy_implication: Evaluate reviewed MLS stack for future groups, not custom crypto
limitations: MLS alone does not deliver radio routing or solve endpoint compromise

title: SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 — Recommendation for Key Management
finding: Key lifecycle, protection, rotation and cryptoperiods must be defined
rust_boy_implication: Device identity onboarding, revocation and offline validity rules must precede alternate links
limitations: Rev. 6 was a draft in Dec 2025; monitor before updating baseline

title: Emergency Communications Guidance Documents and Publications
finding: Interoperability involves SOPs, training, technology, governance and usage
rust_boy_implication: Create human drills and evidence matrix, not only network reconnect tests
limitations: Portal includes evolving materials; archive source version on implementation
